audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash and short-term investments as distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $624.601 million bridge addition, equal to $11.37/share and 23.2% of base equity value; required operating-cash portion unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Our expected short-term and long-term cash needs are primarily for working capital and capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that cash supports seasonal working capital and capital expenditures, but it does not establish the minimum required balance. Treating the entire balance as surplus is therefore an unresolved assumption rather than a demonstrated $624.601 million error. Because the full addition is large relative to the $2.697 billion base value, even a partial exclusion could materially reduce intrinsic value and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum cash and investments required through the pre-holiday seasonal trough, including inventory commitments, vendor payments and planned capital expenditures, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may perpetuate a temporary tariff burden while omitting a potential refund
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $50 million of incremental tariffs paid in 2025; $78 million of refunds received by June 30, 2026, with $62 million recognized in earnings, including $60 million in cost of sales, and $15 million reducing inventory
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, the outcome of the Company’s matter at the CIT may impact our ability to recover the approximately $50 million in incremental tariffs that we paid in 2025, in addition to the incremental tariffs we have paid in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The refund is no longer merely possible: the latest filing demonstrates receipt and accounting recognition. The FY2025 anchor nevertheless contains tariff costs from the terminated regime, while the June 2026 cash bridge may already contain the refund proceeds. Failing to normalize nonrecurring tariff expense can understate operating value, but adding a normalization or refund asset without removing cash already captured in the bridge can overstate value. Continuing tariffs and expected factory accommodations also prevent treating the entire refund as sustainable OE.
audit_findings.action: Trace the approximately $50 million of 2025 tariffs between 2025 cost of sales and closing inventory; reconcile the $78 million refund to June 2026 cash, earnings and inventory; remove refund income from recurring OE; normalize only costs demonstrably nonrecurring; and rerun both OE and the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The latest owner-earnings anchor appears burdened by noncash impairment losses
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.112 million pre-tax impairment charges: $29.0 million of goodwill and intangible impairments plus $10.1 million of PP&E impairments; after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized $29.0 million of impairment charges for the prAna and Mountain Hardwear trade names and goodwill reporting units.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges are demonstrated and equal a large amount relative to the $147.5 million anchor, but the record does not establish whether the OE calculation added them back. If retained, noncash write-downs materially depress the projected numerator. Conversely, repeated brand and store impairments are evidence of economic capital destruction that may warrant a lower growth or reinvestment assessment even when the accounting charges are added back.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE line by line to net income and the cash-flow impairment addback; rerun OE after adding back only noncash charges not already reversed, while separately reflecting recurring store losses or capital destruction in sustainable OE or growth assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Short-term investments may include assets matched by a deferred-compensation claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.686 million of June 30, 2026 short-term money-market and mutual-fund investments, equal to about $0.05/share and 0.10% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: Investments held as part of the Company's deferred compensation plan are recorded at fair value with any gains and losses included in Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A expenses"); a corresponding deferred compensation liability adjustment is recorded separately, resulting in no overall net effect on the Company’s Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish that these investment types are held against deferred-compensation obligations, so including the asset without its matched participant claim overstates shareholder value. The demonstrated amount is only about $0.05 per diluted share versus the $49.10 base value and cannot materially change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Exclude the $2.686 million matched investments from cash/STI or deduct the corresponding current participant liability in the next bridge update; no full DCF rerun is necessary.

audit_findings.title: A discrete FY2025 tax benefit may inflate sustainable owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: One filed favorable tax item is $2.860 million; if fully removed from OE, the computed base-value effect is approximately $0.73/share; the total foreign-currency and deferred-tax revaluation benefit is unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective income tax rate decreased primarily due to a non-recurring expense related to a valuation allowance included in the year ended December 31, 2024, as well as a tax benefit associated with foreign currency losses and a revaluation of deferred tax assets included in the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 tax expense benefited from foreign-currency losses and deferred-tax revaluation, but it does not separately quantify the complete benefit. The identifiable $2.860 million item is only 1.9% of the $147.5 million anchor and would not be material alone, but the record cannot establish whether it represents the entire adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-provision workpaper or footnote reconciliation separating the foreign-currency-loss and deferred-tax-revaluation benefits, substitute a sustainable cash tax rate in FY2025 OE, and rerun if the total adjustment is materially larger than $2.860 million.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed residual D&A pools are approximately $55.8 million in FY2021, $54.6 million in FY2022 and $58.1 million in FY2023; eligible portions are unquantified; direct current-model effect is $0
audit_findings.mechanism: historical OE series and growth assessment
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $59.7m (51.7% of filed D&A); FY2022 $62.6m (53.4% of filed D&A); FY2023 $69.0m (54.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The residual treatment is conservative and could understate historical OE, but the supplied residuals relate to 2021-2023. Those years do not set the current $147.5 million anchor: the computed trend is already $218 million and the method caps the anchor at latest actual OE. Even reclassifying the entire historical residual pools would therefore not change the current anchor or scenario calculations; only evidence affecting FY2025 or the selected growth assumptions could change value.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from the cited historical years for record quality, but rerun the valuation only if filed evidence identifies eligible FY2025 residual D&A or demonstrates that the corrected history changes the independently selected growth cases.
